title: Visnupurana, book 4 (Pathak's critical edition)
source: sa_viSNupurANa-crit.txt; GRETIL (gretil.sub.uni-goettingen.de), CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (data entry: Peter Schreiner)
reply:
Reading the sequence as father-to-son chain: each "tasmāt/tataḥ" gives descent. The text says "jarāsaṃdhasutāt sahadevāt" (Sahadeva, son of Jarāsaṃdha). Later items use "tasya putraḥ", "tasmāt", "tataḥ", and I treat these as son_of where the text implies birth. I give son_of for the explicit "putra"/"tanaya"/"suta" statements and for the ablative-of-origin chain, and I do not add succeeded, since the text says nothing about reigning order beyond birth.

For the ablative chain (tasmāt, tataḥ), I take it as son_of, flagged doubt:false because this is the standard genealogical idiom.

Chain: Sahadeva > Somāpi > Śrutavān > Ayutāyus > Niramitra > Sukṣatra > Bṛhatkarmā > Senajit > Śrutaṃjaya > Vipra > Śucināman > Kṣemya > Suvrata > Dharma > Suśrama > Dṛḍhasena > Sumati > Subala > Sunīta > Satyajit > Viśvajit > Ripuṃjaya.
